message.content:
I’m afraid I don’t have a built‑in function that talks to VirusTotal’s Graphs endpoint, so I can’t fetch those IDs automatically right now.  
Below you’ll find a quick “how‑to” guide – just copy/paste into your own script or terminal – that shows exactly how you’d pull up to eight graph IDs that contain the IP `145.34.45.56`, starting at whatever page (`cursor`) you choose.

---

### 1️⃣ What you need

| Item | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **API Key** | `api_key_2` (replace with your real key) |
| **Endpoint** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/graphs/ip/{ip}` |
| **Parameters** | `limit=8&cursor=cursor_b` |

> ⚠️ *VirusTotal uses OAuth‑style authentication.*  
> You pass the key in the header:

```
x-apikey: <YOUR_API_KEY>
Accept: application/json
```


---

### 2️⃣ Example with cURL

```bash
curl -X GET \
     https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/graphs/ip/145.34.45.56 \
     -H "x-apikey: api_key_2" \
     -G --data-urlencode "limit=8" \
          --data-urlencode "cursor=cursor_b"
```

*If you’re on Windows PowerShell, replace `--data-urlencode` with `-d`.*

This will return JSON similar to:

```json
{
  "meta": { ... },
  "links": {
    "self": "...",
    "next": "...",
    ...
  },
  "data": [
      {"id":"graph_id_001","attributes":{"..."}},
      {"id":"graph_id_002","attributes":{"..."}}
      /* …up to 8 items */
  ]
}
```

Just grab the `"id"` fields inside each object.



---  

### 3️⃣ Quick Python Snippet

```python
import requests

IP   = "145.34.45.56"
KEY  = "api_key_2"
CURSOR = "cursor_b"

url = f"https://www.virustool.com/api/v3/graphs/ip/{IP}"
headers = {
    "x-apikey": KEY,
    "accept": "application/json"
}

params = {
    "limit": 8,
    "cursor": CURSOR
}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
resp.raise_for_status()
results = resp.json()

for item in results["data"]:
    print(item["id"])
```

Replace `requests` import line with `http.client` or other library if you prefer.



---  

### 4️⃣ Pagination / Cursor Notes

* If you hit the end of the list, the response contains a `"next"` link under `"links.next"`.  
* To continue fetching more pages, simply change the value of `cursor=` to the new token returned in that link.  
* Setting `cursor=cursor_b` tells VT to start after the record identified by that cursor ID—useful when resuming a long scan job.



That’s all! Once you run either the cURL or Python sample above, you’ll see the first eight graph IDs that include the target IP. Let me know if you hit any snags while wiring this up.
